title_prefix: -logips is dropped and peer addresses ar
mechanism: "logips" is a DEFINE-CORE-ONLY-OPTIONS row (src/config-options.lisp:444): accepted, named once in the startup WARN, never read. There is no fLogIPs equivalent anywhere -- grep over src/ finds "logips" only in that one table row -- and no logging call takes an address-gating flag. Core at d3056bc keeps the address out of routine peer logging in two independent ways: (1) fLogIPs = GetBoolArg("-logips", DEFAULT_LOGIPS) with DEFAULT_LOGIPS false (src/logging.h:28, src/logging.cpp:47, src/init/common.cpp:34,57), and CNode::LogIP(bool) returns " peeraddr=<addr>" only when it is on while CNode::DisconnectMsg(bool) is just "disconnecting peer=<id>" plus that (src/net.cpp:704-716); (2) every routine per-peer line that calls them is LogDebug(BCLog::NET), so it is not in the default log at all -- 20 call sites in net.cpp and net_processing.cpp pass fLogIPs, and CNode's constructor branches on it to print "Added connection to <addr> peer=N" versus "Added connection peer=N" (src/net.cpp:4004-4009). Ours prints the address unconditionally at :info or :warn, which *current-log-level* admits by default (src/logging.lisp:67, defvar *current-log-level* :info). Counted mechanically over src/: 34 log-info/log-warn/log-error call sites take (peer-address peer) -- 14 in src/networking/ibd.lisp, 13 in src/networking/peer.lisp, 3 in src/node/eviction.lisp, 2 in src/node/peers.lisp, 1 each in src/networking/protocol.lisp and src/node/listen.lisp. Two of them are ROUTINE rather than exceptional: src/node/listen.lisp:44 logs "Inbound peer <addr> (<user-agent>) handshake complete" at :info for every accepted inbound connection, and :30 logs the address of every inbound connection dropped as banned/discouraged. Even our port of Core's own gated line keeps the address: src/networking/peer.lisp:337 is (log-cat "net" "Added connection to ~A peer=~A" host ...), where Core drops the host when fLogIPs is off. One correction to the finding's wording: Core's default log is not perfectly address-free -- net.cpp:388 ("Failed to open new connection to %s, already connected") and net.cpp:1787 ("connection from %s dropped: non-selectable socket") are LogInfo with an address and no gate -- but both are exceptional paths, and neither changes the mechanism.
consequence: The default debug.log of an inbound-listening node becomes a dated record of every address that connected to it and every address it dialed, which Core deliberately made opt-in. Debug logs are the file operators attach to bug reports, hand to support and keep in backups, so the disclosure is of third parties (the node's clients), not only of the operator. The dimension's mitigation does not reach this row at all, and that is what raises it above the other five: the divergence is at Core's DEFAULT, so the operator supplies no option, SUPPLIED-CORE-ONLY-OPTIONS returns nothing, and no warning is printed. There is also no way to turn it off -- -logips=0 is accepted and ignored, and the sites are at :info/:warn so raising -loglevel cannot suppress them without suppressing the log. Bounded only in that it is disclosure to whoever reads the log, not remote leakage; graded S2 rather than S3 because the operator's privacy model is wrong with no warning and no off switch.
evidence: Executed in the project container (worktree /Users/sen/common-lisp/bl-ga11v-options-s3, warm image, probe ga11probe/p-logips.lisp). (a) A real code path writes the address to the log file at the default level: a peer with :address "203.0.113.77:8333" :state :handshaking :connect-time 1 driven through BL.NET::CHECK-HANDSHAKE-TIMEOUT (src/networking/peer.lisp:1479-1491) with *log-file-stream* bound to a string stream and *current-log-level* at its default :info produced exactly "[2026-09-05 12:28:04] [warning] Handshake timeout for peer 203.0.113.77:8333 (292.9s elapsed)". (b) Option contract: (bl.cfg::core-only-option-p "logips") => T, and START-NODE-PLIST on ("-regtest" "-logips=1" "-shrinkdebugfile=0" "-dns=0" "-privatebroadcast=1" "-addresstype=bech32m" "-changetype=bech32m" "-avoidpartialspends=1") returned the plist (:LISTEN T :WALLET-NAMES NIL :NETWORK :REGTEST) -- none of the seven reaches a keyword -- with SUPPLIED-CORE-ONLY-OPTIONS = ("logips" "shrinkdebugfile" "dns" "privatebroadcast" "addresstype" "changetype" "avoidpartialspends"). (c) Call-site census run inside the image over the mounted source: 13 :info/:warn/:error sites in src/networking/peer.lisp take (peer-address peer), 34 across src/ (counts by file above). Sources: src/config-options.lisp:444; src/logging.lisp:67, :288-323, :467-481; src/networking/peer.lisp:337, 448, 620, 626, 654, 675, 1129, 1134, 1190, 1199, 1246, 1260, 1487, 1510; src/node/listen.lisp:30, 44; src/node/init.lisp:1664-1668; refs/bitcoin/src/logging.h:28,35; refs/bitcoin/src/logging.cpp:47; refs/bitcoin/src/init/common.cpp:34,57,102; refs/bitcoin/src/net.cpp:559, 704-716, 1659, 1719, 2865, 3655, 3815-3846, 4004-4009; refs/bitcoin/src/net_processing.cpp:1594, 2380-2428, 2940.
fix_shape: Port fLogIPs as a special (bl.log:*log-ips*, default NIL) set from a new real DEFINE-OPTION "logips" row threaded through start-node the way -logtimestamps and -logthreadnames already are, and port Core's two helpers next to it: a LOG-IP function returning " peeraddr=<addr>" or "", and a DISCONNECT-MSG function returning "disconnecting peer=<id>" plus LOG-IP. Then rewrite the 34 call sites to name the peer by its numeric id -- we already carry PEER-ID -- and append the address only through LOG-IP, which is exactly Core's shape and keeps the line greppable by the functional tests. Where Core additionally routes the line to LogDebug(BCLog::NET) (every DisconnectMsg site, and the CNode-constructor "Added connection" line), move ours to (log-cat "net" ...) at the same time; src/networking/peer.lisp:337 is already log-cat and only needs the host dropped when the flag is off. Do not special-case the two Core LogInfo lines that do print an address (net.cpp:388, :1787) -- match them. A test should drive CHECK-HANDSHAKE-TIMEOUT and the inbound-handshake-complete path with *log-file-stream* bound to a string stream, assert the address is absent by default and present under *log-ips*, and use the flag-on case as the positive control so the assertion cannot pass because the line stopped being emitted.
